> **What this case shows** — the ordinary mean RR is pulled up by the long intervals of a skewed HRV
> distribution; the median throws away everything but the middle. The **trimmed mean** is the robust
> in-between — drop the extreme fraction, average the rest. This case adds one (**`trimmedMean`**),
> completing the robust toolkit (a robust *location* to go with the robust dispersion of `medianAbsDev`
> and `interquartileRange`). On real Fantasia RR it reproduces **scipy.stats.trim_mean** *and* base R
> **`mean(trim=)`** **bit-for-bit**, and it lands neatly between the mean (767 ms) and the median (756 ms).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `trimmedMean(x, trim = 0.1)` → a robust central value.
**Way of thinking** — report location as a family, not a point. The mean (trim 0), a trimmed mean, and the
median (trim → 0.5) bracket how much the tail is pulling your estimate. On a skewed series they separate;
the gap is the signal.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::trimmedMean()`, alongside `medianAbsDev()` and `interquartileRange()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real Fantasia RR intervals, the new `trimmedMean` reproduces both `scipy.stats.trim_mean` and base R
`mean(x, trim)` bit-for-bit (10%-trimmed = 762 ms, `|diff|` = 0 against each); and on the right-skewed RR
the plain mean (767) exceeds the 10%-trimmed (762), which exceeds the 20%-trimmed (760), which exceeds the
median (756).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a progression: the ecosystem had robust dispersion but no robust location —
can a new op reproduce the two references exactly, and where does the trimmed mean sit on a skewed RR
series?** The goal is to introduce `trimmedMean`, certify it against both, and read the mean → trimmed →
median progression.

## Challenge & approach

The trimmed mean discards the `floor(n·trim)` most extreme values from each end and averages the rest — an
order-statistic operation, so it matches any correct implementation exactly. We check `trim = 0.1` against
`scipy.stats.trim_mean` and base R `mean(x, trim)`, and compare the trimmed means with the plain mean and
the median.

```
Fantasia RR (391 intervals) → trimmedMean(trim=0.1) → 762 ms
                            vs scipy.stats.trim_mean → |diff| = 0   ·   vs base R mean(trim) → |diff| = 0
                            mean 767 > trim 0.1 = 762 > trim 0.2 = 760 > median 756   (right-skew)
```

## Data

**Fantasia (PhysioNet)**: subject **f1y01** (young healthy adult), first **5-minute RR window** (391
intervals) — the same RR the [iqr-hrv](../iqr-hrv-fantasia/index.qmd) and
[poincare-hrv](../poincare-hrv-fantasia/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the RR histogram — the mean (767, red dashed) is pulled right of the median (756, blue) by the long-interval tail, with the 10%-trimmed mean (762, orange) in between. Right: the trimmed mean as a function of the trim fraction — it slides smoothly from the ordinary mean (trim 0) down toward the median (trim → 0.5), the 10% point marked; the trimmed mean is a whole family of robust locations.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — mean right of median is the mark of positive skew; the trimmed mean sits
between them. Right — increasing the trim fraction walks the estimate from mean to median; how fast it
falls tells you how heavy the tail is.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **10%-trimmed mean** (`trimmedMean`) | **762 ms** |
| 20%-trimmed mean | 760 ms |
| vs `scipy.stats.trim_mean` / base R `mean(trim)` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-for-bit) |
| plain mean | 767 ms |
| median | 756 ms |

The new op equals both references exactly, and the trimmed mean interpolates between mean and median.
Values trace to [`artifacts/trimmed_summary.csv`](artifacts/trimmed_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`trimmedMean` completes the robust-statistics toolkit — a robust *location* (`trimmedMean`) to sit beside
the robust *dispersion* (`medianAbsDev`, `interquartileRange`) and the classical moments
(`signalMoments`). The transferable takeaway: **on a skewed RR series, report the mean, a trimmed mean,
and the median together. The plain mean overstates the central heart period because the long-interval tail
pulls it up; the trimmed mean discards that tail and lands closer to the typical beat, and the gap between
them is a direct readout of the skew.**

## Open questions

- The trimmed mean is a family indexed by the trim fraction — mean at 0, median at 0.5. The fraction that
  best balances efficiency and robustness for RR depends on the ectopy rate; reporting the trimmed mean
  with the mean and median (as here), or choosing the trim from the observed tail heaviness, makes the
  estimate explicit about its robustness. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Trimmed mean (robust location) | `trimmedMean()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Robust dispersion (MAD, IQR) | `medianAbsDev()`, `interquartileRange()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Classical mean / SD / skewness | `signalMoments()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **trimmed mean** — a central value that ignores the extreme `trim` fraction; on RR it resists ectopic
  beats and long pauses.
- **mean vs trimmed vs median** — all three equal ⇒ symmetric distribution; mean above the trimmed mean
  above the median ⇒ a right tail is inflating the mean.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

trimmedMean(rr, trim = 0.1)          # robust central heart period (ms)
c(mean(rr), trimmedMean(rr, 0.1), median(rr))   # the mean -> trimmed -> median progression
# trimmedMean reproduces scipy.stats.trim_mean and base R mean(trim) bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/trimmed_summary.csv`](artifacts/trimmed_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
trimmed means, the bit-exact match against scipy and base R, the mean > trimmed > median ordering, and the
honestly noted scope (new robust-location op; double-reference machine precision; the skew progression).
